Q79980: Holy Hindu city on the Ganges in Uttar Pradesh, also called Benares or Kashi; one of the oldest inhabited cities in the world.
Pilgrims bathe at its riverside ghats; Hindus believe dying here brings release from rebirth, so cremations burn at Manikarnika Ghat.
The Buddha gave his first sermon at nearby Sarnath.
Known for Banarasi silk saris and Hindustani classical music.
Q3718: Capital of Senegal, on the Cap-Vert peninsula — the westernmost point of mainland Africa.
Capital of French West Africa from 1902.
Gorée Island, offshore, is a memorial to the Atlantic slave trade and a World Heritage Site.
Known for the African Renaissance Monument and as the old finish of the Paris–Dakar Rally.
Q583619: Capital of Imo State in Nigeria's Igbo heartland.
Nicknamed the 'Heartland' and, for its nightlife and hotels, the 'entertainment capital' of Nigeria.
Grew rapidly after becoming the state capital in 1976.
Q217432: Capital of Rivers State, in the oil-rich Niger Delta; the centre of Nigeria's oil industry.
Founded by the British in 1912 to export coal from Enugu; named after colonial secretary Lewis Harcourt.
Has suffered from oil pollution and soot ('black soot').
Q163798: City in central Kerala, called the 'cultural capital of Kerala'.
Built around a hill with the Vadakkunnathan Temple at its centre.
Famous for Thrissur Pooram, a temple festival with dozens of decorated elephants and fireworks.
Former capital of the Kingdom of Cochin.
Q64: Capital of Germany on the Spree; the largest city in the European Union by population within city limits.
Divided by the Berlin Wall from 1961 until it fell in 1989; reunified as the capital in 1990.
Landmarks include the Brandenburg Gate, the Reichstag and Museum Island (a World Heritage Site).
Also one of Germany's 16 federal states.
Q38283: Japan's second-largest city, on Tokyo Bay south of Tokyo, in Kanagawa Prefecture.
A small fishing village until it became one of the first ports opened to foreign trade in 1859.
Japan's first railway (1872) ran between Yokohama and Tokyo; hosted the 2002 FIFA World Cup final.
Q3844: Capital of the Republic of the Congo, on the Congo River directly opposite Kinshasa.
Named after the explorer Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza, who founded it in 1880.
Capital of Free France (de Gaulle's government in exile) in 1940–42 and of French Equatorial Africa.
Brazzaville and Kinshasa are the closest pair of capital cities in the world (apart from Rome and the Vatican).
Q2933: Capital of Paraguay, on the Paraguay River opposite Argentina.
Founded in 1537: one of the oldest cities in South America, called the 'Mother of Cities' because expeditions from here founded others, including Buenos Aires (second time).
Most residents speak both Spanish and Guaraní.
Its metro area holds about a third of Paraguay's people.
Q319660: Capital of Kasai-Oriental province in DR Congo, one of the country's largest cities.
A centre of diamond mining: the region produces a large share of the world's industrial diamonds.
The name means 'goat water' in the Tshiluba language.
Very remote, with few paved roads connecting it to the rest of the country.
Q36529: Capital of Alborz province, about 40 km west of Tehran at the foot of the Alborz mountains.
Iran's fourth-largest city; grew rapidly as an industrial and commuter city for Tehran.
Was a stage on the old road from Tehran to Qazvin.
Has a very diverse population of migrants from all over Iran.
Q5083: The largest city in the US Pacific Northwest, between Puget Sound and Lake Washington.
Home of Amazon and Starbucks; Microsoft and Boeing grew up in the area.
The Space Needle was built for the 1962 World's Fair; Pike Place Market is one of the oldest public markets in the US.
Known for rain, coffee culture and grunge music (Nirvana, Pearl Jam).
Q23958347: Town in Dhaka District, part of the Greater Dhaka conurbation.
Site of the National Martyrs' Memorial, honouring those who died in the 1971 Liberation War.
A centre of the garment industry; the Rana Plaza factory collapse here in 2013 killed over 1,100 workers.
Q1113311: Capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, near the Khyber Pass to Afghanistan.
One of the oldest cities in South Asia; as Purushapura it was capital of the Kushan Empire.
For centuries a trading post on the route between Central Asia and India; its Qissa Khwani ('storytellers') Bazaar is famous.
Q12439: The largest city in Michigan, on the Detroit River across from Windsor, Canada.
The 'Motor City': birthplace of the American car industry (Ford, General Motors, Chrysler).
Gave its name to the Motown record label and soul sound; also a birthplace of techno.
Lost more than half its population after 1950 and went bankrupt in 2013, but has been recovering.
Q3777: Capital of Burkina Faso; often shortened to 'Ouaga'.
Traditional seat of the Mossi kings (Moro Naba), whose ceremony is still held every Friday.
Hosts FESPACO, Africa's largest film festival, held every two years.
Also hosts SIAO, a major African crafts fair.
Q3881: Capital of Zambia, on a plateau at about 1,280 m.
Founded in 1905 as a railway siding and village; became the capital of Northern Rhodesia in 1935.
Named after a local chief, Lusaaka.
One of the fastest-growing cities in southern Africa.
Q373346: The largest prefecture-level city in Shandong by area and population.
Has one of China's largest wholesale and logistics markets.
Wang Xizhi, China's most famous calligrapher, was born here; the Yinqueshan Han tombs held a lost copy of Sun Tzu's Art of War.
The name means 'next to the Yi River'.
Q59173: City in Guangdong on Daya Bay, northeast of Shenzhen and about 70 km from Hong Kong.
Its West Lake is famous for the Song poet Su Dongpo, who was exiled here.
Home to TCL, a big electronics maker.
Q171617: City in São Paulo state, about 90 km northwest of São Paulo.
Grew rich in the 19th-century coffee boom.
Home of the University of Campinas (Unicamp), one of Brazil's top universities, and a big tech industry cluster.
Its Viracopos airport is a major cargo hub.
Q16520: South Korea's second city and main port, at the southeastern tip of the Korean Peninsula.
During the Korean War it was one of the few cities not captured by the North and served as temporary capital.
Known for Haeundae Beach, the hillside Gamcheon Culture Village and Jagalchi fish market.
Hosts the Busan International Film Festival, Asia's most important.
Q66616: The largest city of Madhya Pradesh, in central India.
Ruled by the Holkar dynasty of the Marathas; Queen Ahilyabai Holkar is still revered.
Ranked India's cleanest city in national surveys every year since 2017.
Famous for its street food, e.g. at Sarafa night market.
Q79923: Puebla, capital of the Mexican state of the same name, was founded by the Spanish in 1531 between Mexico City and Veracruz.
Its historic centre with colourful Talavera-tiled buildings is a World Heritage Site.
Origin of mole poblano sauce and chiles en nogada.
The Battle of Puebla (5 May 1862) against the French is the origin of Cinco de Mayo; the Great Pyramid of Cholula is nearby.
Q311544: The metropolitan municipality of Durban and surrounding towns in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
Created in 2000; most of its people speak isiZulu.
Durban's port is the busiest in sub-Saharan Africa.
Q183584: Capital of Gansu province, on the Yellow River in northwestern China.
A major stop on the Silk Road and gateway to the Hexi Corridor leading west.
The first iron bridge over the Yellow River, Zhongshan Bridge (1909), is here.
Q198370: Its Linzi district was Linzi, capital of the ancient state of Qi and one of the biggest cities of its time.
Considered a birthplace of cuju, the ancient Chinese football game.
Famous since 2023 for its barbecue, which attracted crowds from all over China; the writer Pu Songling was born here.
Q16552: City on the Pacific in Southern California, right next to the Mexican border and Tijuana.
Called the 'Birthplace of California': the first Spanish mission in California was founded here in 1769.
Home of a large US Navy base and the famous San Diego Zoo.
Known for its mild climate, beaches and Balboa Park.
Q62: City on a peninsula between the Pacific and San Francisco Bay, crossed by the Golden Gate Bridge.
Grew from a small settlement into a city during the California Gold Rush of 1849.
Largely destroyed by the 1906 earthquake and fire.
Known for cable cars, Alcatraz, Chinatown, LGBT history and the nearby Silicon Valley tech industry.
Q80484: Capital of Bihar on the south bank of the Ganges.
As Pataliputra it was the capital of the Maurya Empire under Ashoka and of the Gupta Empire.
Birthplace of the tenth Sikh Guru, Gobind Singh; Bodh Gaya and Nalanda are nearby.
One of the oldest continuously inhabited places in the world.
Q5468: South Africa's third city and main port, on the Indian Ocean in KwaZulu-Natal.
Has the largest Indian community in Africa — Gandhi lived in the region as a young lawyer.
Known for its warm beaches, surfing, and 'bunny chow' (curry in a hollowed-out loaf).
Formerly named Port Natal; renamed after governor Benjamin D'Urban.
Q68695: Port city in southern Fujian on the Taiwan Strait.
Known to medieval traders as Zaiton, it was one of the largest ports in the world; Marco Polo and Ibn Battuta praised it.
A World Heritage Site as an 'Emporium of the World', with Hindu, Muslim and Buddhist relics side by side.
Today a centre of shoe and sportswear makers (Anta, Xtep) in Jinjiang.
Q1513: The largest city of central India, in Maharashtra; called the 'Orange City' for its orange farming.
Founded in 1702 by a Gond king; later capital of the Bhonsle Marathas and of the Central Provinces.
Lies near the geographic centre of India — the 'Zero Mile Stone' marks it.
Here B. R. Ambedkar converted to Buddhism with hundreds of thousands of followers in 1956.
Q3561: Capital of Algeria, on the Mediterranean; called 'Alger la Blanche' for its white buildings.
Its Casbah, the old Ottoman-era citadel, is a World Heritage Site.
A base of the Barbary corsairs; capital of French Algeria from 1830 to 1962.
Scene of the Battle of Algiers (1956–57) in the war of independence; the Notre-Dame d'Afrique and the Great Mosque of Algiers are landmarks.
Q43509: Ecuador's largest city and main port, on the Guayas River near the Pacific.
Ecuador's economic capital, while Quito in the Andes is the political capital.
Known for its riverside promenade, the Malecón 2000, and the Las Peñas hillside quarter.
Gateway for many trips to the Galápagos Islands.
Q187136: City in western Henan at the confluence of the Luo and Yellow rivers.
One of China's Four Great Ancient Capitals, capital of 13 dynasties.
The Longmen Grottoes, with about 100,000 Buddhist statues carved in cliffs, are a World Heritage Site.
The White Horse Temple is considered the first Buddhist temple in China; famous for its peony festival.
Q3037: Capital of Nepal, at about 1,400 m in the Kathmandu Valley.
Historically the centre of the Newar people; the valley has seven World Heritage monuments, incl. Durbar Square, Swayambhunath and Boudhanath.
A starting point for treks in the Himalayas.
Q1555: Capital of Guatemala, the largest city in Central America, in a highland valley.
Founded in 1776 after an earthquake destroyed the old capital, Antigua Guatemala.
The Maya city of Kaminaljuyu lay on its site.
Surrounded by active volcanoes such as Pacaya and Volcán de Fuego.
Q10396: City in West Java directly south of Jakarta, part of the Jakarta metropolitan area.
Home to the main campus of the University of Indonesia.
Its founder, the Dutch landowner Cornelis Chastelein, freed his slaves in 1714 and left them his land.
Q18808: Capital of North Korea, on the Taedong River.
One of Korea's oldest cities; capital of the ancient Goguryeo kingdom.
Almost completely destroyed in the Korean War and rebuilt in Soviet monumental style.
Landmarks: Kim Il Sung Square, the Juche Tower and the unfinished 105-storey Ryugyong Hotel.
Q57719: City in northwestern Jiangsu where four provinces meet; historically called Pengcheng.
Hometown of Liu Bang, founder of the Han dynasty; rich Han tombs and terracotta warriors were found here.
A key railway crossing of the Beijing–Shanghai and east–west lines.
Site of the decisive Huaihai Campaign of the Chinese Civil War (1948–49).
Q216075: The largest city of the Mekong Delta in southern Vietnam, on the Hậu River.
Famous for its floating markets, like Cái Răng, where traders sell from boats.
The Cần Thơ Bridge across the Mekong was finished in 2010.
Became much larger in 2025 when two neighbouring provinces were merged into it.
Q490: Capital of Lombardy and Italy's economic capital; its metro area is the largest in Italy.
Founded by Celts; as Mediolanum it was capital of the Western Roman Empire (286–402).
A world fashion and design capital and home of La Scala opera house.
Leonardo da Vinci's 'Last Supper' and the Gothic Duomo are here; co-host of the 2026 Winter Olympics.
Q3889: Capital of Mozambique, on Maputo Bay of the Indian Ocean.
Called Lourenço Marques under Portuguese rule, until 1976.
Known for its jacaranda trees, Art Deco and modernist architecture, and the iron house attributed to Eiffel's workshop.
A key port for South Africa's Gauteng region.
Q581999: Twin city in the Mumbai metropolitan region, in Thane district.
Kalyan is an old port town with over 700 years of history.
Kalyan Junction is one of the busiest railway junctions on Mumbai's suburban network.
Q58570: City in southern Hebei, one of the oldest cities in China, settled about 8,500 years ago.
Capital of the Zhao state during the Warring States period.
The origin of many Chinese idioms; known for Cishan culture finds and the Xiangtangshan Buddhist grottoes.
Q9885: Tamil Nadu's second city, at the foot of the Western Ghats; called the 'Manchester of South India' for its textile mills.
Lies at the Palakkad Gap, the old trade route between Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
Known for pumps, motors and engineering industries.
Gateway to the hill station Ooty and the Isha Foundation's giant Adiyogi Shiva statue.
Q1524: Capital of Greece and one of the oldest cities in the world, with over 3,400 years of recorded history.
Birthplace of democracy and centre of classical Greek philosophy (Socrates, Plato, Aristotle).
The Acropolis with the Parthenon is a World Heritage Site.
Hosted the first modern Olympics in 1896 and again in 2004.
Q57818: City in Jiangsu on the Grand Canal and the Huai River, the traditional boundary between northern and southern China.
Birthplace of Zhou Enlai, China's first premier, and of Wu Cheng'en, author of 'Journey to the West'.
Known for Huaiyang cuisine, one of China's major cooking styles.
Q34261: Capital of Haiti, on the Gulf of Gonâve.
Founded by the French in 1749; Haiti became the first independent Black republic in 1804 after a slave revolt.
Devastated by the 2010 earthquake, which killed over 200,000 people.
Large parts have been controlled by armed gangs in recent years.
Q170688: Bolivia's largest city, in the tropical eastern lowlands.
Founded in 1561 by Ñuflo de Chávez and moved several times before settling on the Piraí River.
The country's economic engine, with agribusiness (soy) and natural gas.
Very different from the Andean highland cities like La Paz in climate and culture ('camba' culture).
Q243322: City in Punjab, Pakistan, north of Lahore; nicknamed the 'City of Wrestlers'.
Birthplace of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, founder of the Sikh Empire, and its first capital.
One of Pakistan's main industrial centres, known for ceramics, fans and metal goods.
Q11909: City in Gujarat, also called Baroda, on the Vishwamitri River.
Capital of the princely state of Baroda under the Gaekwad dynasty.
The Laxmi Vilas Palace is said to be four times the size of Buckingham Palace.
Called the 'cultural capital' of Gujarat; home of Maharaja Sayajirao University.
Q1475: The most populous city of the Philippines, part of Metro Manila.
Founded in 1939 and named after President Manuel L. Quezon; capital of the Philippines from 1948 to 1976.
Home of the University of the Philippines and many TV networks.
The 1986 People Power Revolution took place on EDSA avenue, partly in Quezon City.
Q321475: Ancient port city in southern Kerala on Ashtamudi Lake; formerly called Quilon.
A spice port for over 2,000 years, trading with Romans, Arabs and Chinese.
Q167715: Capital of Kerala, near India's southern tip; formerly called Trivandrum.
Capital of the Kingdom of Travancore.
The Padmanabhaswamy Temple held a hidden treasure worth billions, discovered in 2011.
Home of the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, India's main rocket development centre.
Q58584: City in central Hebei, about 150 km southwest of Beijing.
Seat of the Viceroy of Zhili (the province around Beijing) during the Qing dynasty.
Known for Baoding iron balls and donkey-meat burgers.
Home of the carmaker Great Wall Motors.
Q217698: City in central Shandong; the 'World Kite Capital'.
Hosts the Weifang International Kite Festival every April and has a kite museum.
Known for its Yangjiabu woodblock New Year prints.
Shandong's agricultural vegetable hub at Shouguang is in the prefecture.
Q187593: DR Congo's second-largest city, in the far southeast near Zambia; formerly Élisabethville.
Centre of the Copperbelt: copper and cobalt mining (cobalt is key for batteries).
Was the capital of Moïse Tshombe's breakaway State of Katanga (1960–63).
Home of the football club TP Mazembe.
Q20934: Port city west of Seoul; South Korea's third-largest city.
Incheon International Airport is South Korea's main gateway and one of the world's busiest.
General MacArthur's 1950 Inchon landing turned the tide of the Korean War.
Has Korea's only official Chinatown and the planned Songdo smart city; hosted the 2014 Asian Games.
Q1467: Capital of Cebu province in the Visayas; the oldest city of the Philippines.
Magellan landed here in 1521 and planted a cross (Magellan's Cross) — and was killed by chief Lapulapu on nearby Mactan.
The first Spanish settlement in the Philippines (1565) under Legazpi.
The Basilica del Santo Niño holds the oldest Christian relic in the country; the Sinulog festival is held every January.
